# Preface {.unnumbered}

## What this book is

This is a research log and a course at the same time, and it is honest
about being both.

The research is one question about one architecture. QuEra Computing's
*transversal STAR* proposal [@ismail2026transversal; @ismail2026highrate]
is a plan for the first useful fault-tolerant machines — the
"megaquop" regime of about a million reliable operations — in which the
expensive non-Clifford gates are not distilled but *injected*: a small
rotation is applied directly to a handful of physical atoms, and the
attempts that went wrong are thrown away. The reach of that plan is capped
by a single coefficient, α, in the error of each injected rotation. The
papers that propose it fold all physical noise into one knob. This book
asks which physical channel the coefficient actually answers to, and what
halving each one would buy.

The course is everything its author needed to learn to ask that question
properly: what a STAR injection is, algebraically; how a surface-code
memory is decoded; what a neutral-atom machine physically does and how it
fails; and how a rotation budget becomes a simulation. It is written for a
reader who knows quantum circuits and some error correction, and wants to
reach the point where every number in a paper like
@ismail2026transversal can be re-derived at a whiteboard.

## How it keeps itself honest

The book is built around six commitments, each enforced by a program that
fails the build when it is broken. They are listed in `OUTLINE.md`; the
three that shape the reading are these.

**Experiments are pre-registered.** Every measurement in Part III comes from
a protocol committed to git before the measurement existed. A guard reads
the commit history and the date stamped inside every result file, and fails
if a result is older than its protocol. A protocol written afterwards is a
description; only the history can tell the two apart.

**Validation comes before novelty.** The first experiment does not ask
anything new. It asks whether this book's pipeline reproduces the curve
QuEra itself published for these circuits, under QuEra's own noise model.
Nothing later is evidence unless that passes.

**Every chapter discloses its AI use.** This book was written with an AI
coding agent, deliberately and heavily. Each chapter ends its main text with
a 🤖 **Agent Log** stating what the agent did, what the author verified by
hand, and what the agent got wrong. The log is a disclosure, not a badge,
and it is the part of each chapter its author must be able to defend
without notes.

## How to read a chapter

Every chapter keeps the same contract, and `tools/check_structure.py`
checks that it does:

| Box | What it is for |
|---|---|
| 🎯 **Learning Goals** | what you can do at the end that you could not at the start |
| 🧑‍🏫 **Whiteboard** | a derivation to reproduce cold — no notes, no agent |
| 🔬 **Evidence** | a measured number, with shots, interval, seed and environment |
| 🤖 **Agent Log** | delegated · verified by hand · caught |
| 🎤 **Interview Drill** | what someone hiring for this work would ask |
| 💪 **Exercises** | practice that builds the whiteboard skill |

The Whiteboard boxes are the spine. A derivation counts as mastered when it
has been reproduced correctly, on paper, on two different days.

## The inputs this book does not own

The STAR circuits and the reference plot that Part III measures against were
published by QuEra Computing for the ETH QHack 2026 challenge. That
repository carries no license, so this book never redistributes them:
`make fetch` downloads them at one pinned commit and checks every file
against a SHA-256 recorded in `tools/fetch_star_circuits.py`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import hashlib
import pathlib

root = pathlib.Path.cwd()
root = next(p for p in (root, *root.parents) if (p / "starlab").is_dir())
inputs = sorted((root / "data/external/eth_qhack_2026").glob("*"))
print(f"{'fetched input':<22}{'SHA-256 (first 16 hex)':>26}")
for path in inputs:
    digest = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
    print(f"{path.name:<22}{digest:>26}")
```
